abstract: Yale RCT establishing scaling laws for AI-driven productivity gains, finding approximately 8% per year reduction in task completion time, which compounds to roughly 20% productivity improvement per decade. The study provides a quantitative framework for projecting AI's productivity trajectory based on observed improvement rates, offering more grounded estimates than speculation-driven forecasts.
keyFindings: AI reduces task completion time by approximately 8% per year based on observed data
Compounding effect yields roughly 20% productivity improvement per decade
Productivity scaling follows predictable patterns amenable to quantitative projection
RCT design provides stronger causal evidence than observational productivity studies
methodology: Yale randomized controlled trial measuring task completion time reductions from AI assistance across standardized tasks, fitting scaling law models to observed productivity improvement rates over successive AI model generations.
qualifiers: Scaling laws derived from current trends may not hold if AI capability improvements accelerate or plateau. Lab-based task time measurements may not translate directly to real-world productivity gains. 8%/year rate represents an average across task types with significant variation.
